title: US markets closed — Memorial Day (falls INSIDE the FOMC blackout window, the only time in 166 windows)
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule', SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,899 bytes). The 2027 panel is a hidden tab whose text the rendered page drops, so this session parsed it out of the page's own embedded payload, the same method the sibling sifma-bond-early-close-2027-03-25 entry documented: the US 2027 Memorial Day entry renders as heading 'Memorial Day', date 'Monday, May 31, 2027', note 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, May 28, 2027'. Independently reproduced by weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Memorial Day on the LAST Monday in May, and the last Monday of May 2027 is 2027-05-31. The NYSE side is INHERITED, NOT RE-READ: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars returned HTTP 403 to this runner on three attempts with three different user agents on 2026-09-05, where sibling sessions reached it at HTTP 200 (109,180 bytes) earlier the same day and quoted its Memorial Day cell as 'Monday, May 31' — that quote is carried in the fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29 entry's own notes and is the provenance for the equity closure specifically. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the sibling closure entries good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26 and presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and one leg of the evidence (the NYSE cell) is inherited rather than fetched here. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy and the fetch, not the evidence
notes: DISCOVERED during the fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Why a day the market is shut earns a row: it is the ONLY dated non-Fed item inside that blackout window, and the window is itself a first. Measured in that ledger's leg 5 across all 166 FOMC blackout windows derivable from the Board's own footnote rule applied to every parsed meeting 2007-2027, this is the only window that contains Memorial Day — a direct consequence of the eight-day calendar shift fomc-2027-06-09 measured, which pulls the June 2027 gate back into May. THE LEDGER THAT DISCOVERED IT ALSO REFUSED TO BUILD ON IT, and that refusal is the point of this note: a holiday inside a blackout window is routine (MLK falls inside 16 of the 166, Labor Day 5, Good Friday 1, Juneteenth 1), an 8-trading-session window is routine (33 of the 155 measurable windows run 8 sessions; the distribution is 8 -> 33, 9 -> 118, 10 -> 4), and the pre-holiday deadline session the closure creates is measurably ordinary: the 15 MLK-window precedents run 0.765% mean absolute S&P close-to-close move against a 0.742% January baseline, and the pre-Memorial-Day Friday itself runs 0.556% across 21 years (2005-2026 ex-2020) against a 0.698% May baseline — BELOW it. So the honest statement is narrow: the window's first three calendar days contain one trading session, which is a scheduling fact with no measured price consequence. Registered as FT-fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29-3 so the refusal is scoreable rather than merely asserted. WHAT DOES CARRY: the preceding session, Friday 2027-05-28, is the last day any FOMC participant may speak before the gate falls, and SIFMA recommends a 2:00 p.m. ET fixed-income close on it (filed separately as sifma-bond-early-close-2027-05-28) — so the operative Fed deadline is 14:00 ET in the rates market, not the 16:00 equity close. IMPACT LOW AND STRUCTURAL ONLY: a closed session moves nothing by itself and no house playbook is calendar-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped this session for 'holiday|memorial|closure|half-day|early close|blackout': zero hits in both). It widens caution and licenses nothing. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'sector', the same least-wrong choice the Good Friday and Presidents Day siblings documented. DUPLICATE CHECK RUN: the calendar carried no Memorial Day entry for any year before this one, and no second 2027-05-31 entry exists — the presidents-day/washingtons-birthday collision on 2027-02-15 is the precedent that made this check part of the sweep.
